Subject: Renewal + capacity increase: looking to double to 32 GPUs

Hi Stephanie,

We’re preparing our renewal and want to move our Dedicated pool from 16 -> 32 GPUs starting at renewal. Key asks from our side: a committed per-hour reserved rate (we need a number to put into our budget), and a throughput/latency commitment — AtlasAI runs real-time ranking requests so p95/p99 matters.

Can Redwood provide a formal quote with:
- revised per-hour reserved pricing for 32 GPUs (12-month term)
- a throughput guarantee (min sustained vCPU throughput or requests/sec) and what credits you provide if you miss it
- any constraints on bursting or regional placement (we may use multi-region)

We’d like to review this internally next week. Also share any PO/contract lead times.

Thanks,
Jeff

Jeff — thanks for the clear ask. We’d be very excited to support AtlasAI at 32 GPUs. I’ve put together an initial commercial proposal and SLA sketch below for you to review; attaching a PDF with the formal numbers.

High level proposal (12-month term, reserved):
- Reserved capacity: 32 x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Rate: $9.40 per GPU-hour (reserved committed rate) — effective per-hour for the entire reserved pool
- Burst: Allowed up to 15% above reserved hourly capacity for short bursts (no additional charge if within burst window)
- Throughput SLA: 95% of monthly hours where end-to-end p95 latency < 350ms for the configured instance class; if missed, credit 10% of monthly reserved fee for each SLA miss window (cumulative cap 50%)

Notes: This quote assumes model families and token distributions similar to what we discussed during POE. If AtlasAI requires a tighter p99 target or higher availability, we can provide an enhanced SLA (higher credit / tighter targets) and discuss options for geographic redundancy.

Next steps: I’ll loop in Rishi and Neha to confirm the SLA operational details and validate the throughput assumptions. If this looks directionally correct, I’ll send a formal proposal with DocuSign.

Regards,

1) Pricing: $9.40/GPU-hour is higher than we expected. Our target budget was closer to $7.25/GPU-hour committed. Can Redwood bridge that gap?

2) SLA: p95 < 350ms is reasonable, but we actually need assurances on p99 for peak windows (we see spikes during inference-heavy periods). What would it take to get p99 < 700ms with a contractual credit structure?

If we can get closer on price and firm p99 commitments, we can sign quickly — we’re aiming to have this in place before our next model launch in mid-June.

Stephanie / Neha — ran this against our ops deck and infra assumptions. Summary and recommended commercial approach: 

Operational feasibility:
- p99 < 700ms is achievable for AtlasAI’s profile if we provision 32 GPUs with prewarmed KV caches and a 2:1 request sharding rule. For peak hours we recommend enabling adaptive batching but keeping burst headroom at 10-15% to avoid queueing.
- Cross-region failover: we do NOT recommend a single logical reserved pool across two regions for hard SLA guarantees. Best practice: two mirrored reservations (primary + DR) or dedicated multi-region active-active with geo-routing — the latter requires a larger committed footprint and slightly higher price.

Commercial counterproposal (12-month):
- Option A (single-reservation, primary region us-west1): $8.10 per GPU-hour, 32 GPUs reserved, p95 < 350ms guarantee as previously stated. p99 guarantee offered during business hours (Mon-Fri 00:00-20:00 UTC): p99 < 700ms; outside of that window p99 best-effort. SLA credit: 12% monthly reserved fee per missed window, cumulative cap 60%.
- Option B (mirrored-reservations for failover, us-west1 + us-east1): two 16-GPU reservations (32 total across regions) at $8.60 per GPU-hour each. This structure lowers the operational risk for p99 and gives deterministic regional failover. SLA: p99 < 700ms across primary region; failover governed by standard DR runbook. Credit: 10% monthly fee per credible miss, cap 40%.

Upsell/term incentive: 24-month term reduces Option A price to $7.55/GPU-hour and Option B to $8.00/GPU-hour.

If we want to be more aggressive on price for strategic deals, there is room to go to $7.90 (12-month) or $7.25 (24-month) but that should be approved by revenue ops due to margin impact.

I’ll prepare a clean proposal PDF with Option A/B and 12/24 month permutations for Stephanie to send.

—Rishi
